exp.question: What is the factorial of 4 (4!)?
exp.facts: 4! = 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 24. 12 is only 4 x 3, 16 is 4 x 4, and 120 is 5!.

exp.question: What is the negative of iota (i)?
exp.facts: The negative of any number x is -x, so the negative of i is -i. i is the number itself, and 1 and -1 are real numbers, not the negative of i.
exp.rel: i squared = -1, so 1/i = -i. i to the power 4 = 1.

exp.question: Where was Benazir Bhutto assassinated on 27 December 2007?
exp.facts: Benazir Bhutto was killed after an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi. Karsaz in Karachi was the earlier October 2007 attack on her rally, and Garhi Khuda Bakhsh is where she is buried.
exp.rel: Liaquat Ali Khan, the first PM, was also assassinated at the same park in Rawalpindi in 1951.

exp.question: What is 90% of 90?
exp.rel: 10% of a number = the number divided by 10. 50% of 90 = 45.

exp.question: What is one third of one tenth of 90?
exp.facts: One tenth of 90 is 9, and one third of 9 is 3. 9 is only one tenth, 30 is only one third, and 1 is too small.
exp.rel: Of means multiply: (1/3) x (1/10) x 90 = 90/30 = 3.

exp.question: What was the name of the father of Hazrat Khadija (RA)?
exp.facts: Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the daughter of Khuwaylid ibn Asad of the Quraysh. Abu Talib was the Prophet's uncle, Abdul Muttalib his grandfather, and Abu Quhafa the father of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).
exp.rel: Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first wife of the Prophet (PBUH) and the first person to accept Islam. Her title is Tahira.

exp.question: Who married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (2)
exp.facts: Hazrat Uthman (RA) married Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA) and, after her death, Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA), so he is called Dhun-Nurayn (possessor of two lights). Hazrat Ali (RA) married only Hazrat Fatima (RA), and Abu Bakr and Umar (RA) were fathers-in-law of the Prophet.
exp.rel: Hazrat Zainab (RA), the eldest daughter, married Abul As. Hazrat Fatima (RA) married Hazrat Ali (RA).

exp.question: What is the meaning of Al-Ahzab, the name of Surah 33?
exp.facts: Ahzab means the confederates or allied groups, the tribes who joined to attack Madinah in the Battle of the Trench. The Cave is Al-Kahf, the Spoils of War is Al-Anfal, and the Victory is Al-Fath.
exp.rel: The Battle of Ahzab (Khandaq) took place in 5 AH. The trench was suggested by Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA).

exp.question: What is the capital city of Australia?
exp.facts: Canberra is the capital of Australia. Sydney is the largest city, and Melbourne and Perth are other big cities, not the capital.
exp.rel: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand. Ottawa is the capital of Canada.

exp.question: Which is the largest seaport of Pakistan?
exp.facts: Karachi Port is the largest and busiest seaport of Pakistan. Port Qasim is the second largest, Gwadar is a newer deep-sea port under CPEC, and Pasni is a small fishing port.
exp.rel: Port Qasim is also in Karachi. Gwadar Port is in Balochistan.

exp.question: The Eiffel Tower in Paris was completed in which year?
exp.facts: The Eiffel Tower was built from 1887 and completed in 1889 for the World Fair in Paris. 1789 was the French Revolution, and 1901 and 1914 are too late.
exp.rel: It was designed by the company of Gustave Eiffel. The Statue of Liberty (1886) was a gift from France to the USA.

exp.question: Ayat al-Birr (the verse of righteousness) is in which Surah?
exp.facts: Ayat al-Birr is verse 177 of Surah Al-Baqarah; it says righteousness is not turning faces east or west but true faith and good deeds. The other Surahs do not contain this verse.
exp.rel: Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah. Ayat al-Dain (longest verse) is verse 282 of Al-Baqarah.

exp.question: Which animal was with the Ashab-e-Kahf (People of the Cave) in the cave?
exp.facts: Surah Al-Kahf says a dog stretched its forelegs at the entrance of the cave. The Quran mentions no cat, camel or horse with them.
exp.rel: The dog is traditionally named Qitmir. The sleepers stayed in the cave for 309 years (Al-Kahf 18:25).

exp.question: What was the age of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at the time of Hijrat to Madinah?
exp.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) received the first revelation at 40 and spent 13 years preaching in Makkah, so he migrated at 53. 63 was his age at death, and 50 was his age in the Year of Grief.
exp.rel: Hijrat took place in 622 AD; Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was with him in Cave Thawr.

exp.question: Who wrote the book My Brother?
exp.facts: My Brother is a book by Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah about her brother Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah. The Quaid did not write it about himself, and Iqbal and Begum Ra'ana Liaquat did not write it.
exp.rel: Fatima Jinnah is called Madr-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation). The book was published in 1987 by the Quaid-e-Azam Academy.

exp.question: Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in May 1998 at which site?
exp.facts: Pakistan tested its nuclear devices on 28 May 1998 in the Ras Koh Hills of Chagai, Balochistan. Kahuta is the uranium enrichment lab (KRL), Thar is famous for coal, and Kharan was used for the 30 May test only, not the main site.
exp.rel: 28 May is celebrated as Youm-e-Takbeer. Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan founded Khan Research Laboratories (KRL) at Kahuta.

exp.question: Hazrat Hajra (AS) was the mother of which Prophet? (2)
exp.facts: Hazrat Hajra (AS) was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS). Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Sarah (AS), Yaqub (AS) was son of Ishaq, and Yusuf (AS) was son of Yaqub.
exp.rel: Hazrat Hajra (AS) ran between Safa and Marwa searching for water, which is now Sa'i in Hajj. The well of Zamzam appeared for Hazrat Ismail (AS).

exp.question: Which female companion narrated the most Hadith?
exp.facts: Hazrat Aisha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), narrated about 2210 Hadith, the most by any woman. Umm Salama (RA) and Hafsa (RA) narrated far fewer, and Hazrat Fatima (RA) narrated very few.
exp.rel: Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) narrated the most Hadith overall (about 5374). Hazrat Aisha (RA) is called Umm-ul-Momineen and Siddiqa.

exp.question: What is the capital of Somalia?
exp.facts: Mogadishu is the capital and largest city of Somalia, on the Indian Ocean coast. Nairobi is the capital of Kenya, Addis Ababa of Ethiopia, and Djibouti city of Djibouti.
exp.rel: Somalia is in the Horn of Africa. Its currency is the Somali shilling.

exp.question: Who was Bulleh Shah?
exp.facts: Bulleh Shah (1680-1757) was a famous Punjabi Sufi poet. His shrine is in Kasur, Punjab. He was not a king or ruler, and he wrote in Punjabi, not Pashto.
exp.rel: Waris Shah wrote Heer Ranjha in Punjabi. Rehman Baba and Khushal Khan Khattak are famous Pashto poets.

exp.question: Who was the second Khalifa of Islam?
exp.facts: Hazrat Umar Farooq (RA) became the second Khalifa in 634 AD after Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA). Abu Bakr (RA) was the first, Usman (RA) the third and Ali (RA) the fourth.
exp.rel: Hazrat Umar (RA) ruled about 10 years (634-644 AD). He started the Hijri calendar.

exp.question: Who is known as Abu Hafs?
exp.facts: Abu Hafs was the kunya (title) of Hazrat Umar (RA); Hafs means lion cub, and his daughter was Hafsa (RA). Abu Turab was Hazrat Ali's title, and Saifullah was Khalid bin Waleed's title. Abu Bakr is itself a kunya.
exp.rel: Hazrat Umar (RA) was also called Al-Farooq. Hazrat Usman (RA) was called Zun-Nurain.

exp.question: What is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir?
exp.facts: Muzaffarabad is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir, on the Jhelum and Neelum rivers. Mirpur and Rawalakot are other AJK cities, and Srinagar is the summer capital of Indian-held Kashmir.
exp.rel: Gilgit is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan. Mangla Dam is in Mirpur district, AJK.

exp.question: Who was the second Governor-General of Pakistan?
exp.facts: Khawaja Nazimuddin became the second Governor-General in September 1948 after Quaid-e-Azam died. Ghulam Muhammad was the third and Iskander Mirza the fourth (last). Liaquat Ali Khan was the first Prime Minister.
exp.rel: Quaid-e-Azam was the first Governor-General. Khawaja Nazimuddin later became the second Prime Minister in 1951.

exp.question: The Simla (Shimla) Agreement was signed in which year and by whom?
options: 1966, Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri
1972, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi
1999, Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee
1950, Liaquat Ali Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru
exp.facts: The Simla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi after the 1971 war. 1966 was the Tashkent Declaration, 1999 the Lahore Declaration, and 1950 the Liaquat-Nehru Pact.
exp.rel: The ceasefire line in Kashmir was renamed the Line of Control (LoC) under the Simla Agreement. It was signed in Simla, India.

exp.question: On which date were the general elections of 2024 held in Pakistan?
exp.facts: Pakistan's 12th general elections were held on 8 February 2024. 25 July was the date of the 2018 election and 11 May of the 2013 election; 8 March 2024 was not an election day.
exp.rel: Shehbaz Sharif became Prime Minister in March 2024 after this election. The 2018 election was held on 25 July 2018.

exp.question: Choose the synonym of EMINENT.
exp.facts: Eminent means famous and respected, so distinguished is the synonym. Ordinary and hidden are nearly opposites. Imminent is a different word meaning about to happen.
exp.rel: Prominent and renowned are also synonyms of eminent. Antonym: obscure or unknown.

exp.question: Change into indirect speech: The teacher asked, "Who speaks English?"
options: The teacher asked who speaks English.
The teacher asked who spoke English.
The teacher asked that who spoke English.
The teacher asked who had spoken English?
exp.facts: In indirect speech the present tense (speaks) changes to past tense (spoke), and the question word who is kept with no that and no question mark. Option A keeps the present tense, C wrongly adds that, and D uses the wrong tense and a question mark.
exp.rel: Yes/no questions use if or whether: He asked, "Are you ready?" becomes He asked if I was ready. Present continuous changes to past continuous.

exp.question: What are the three degrees of adjectives?
exp.facts: Adjectives have three degrees: positive (tall), comparative (taller) and superlative (tallest). Simple, compound, complex are kinds of sentences, and present, past, future are tenses.
exp.rel: Irregular forms: good, better, best and bad, worse, worst. Long adjectives use more and most (more beautiful, most beautiful).

exp.question: What are the two pieces of the male Ihram called?
exp.facts: The male Ihram is two white unstitched sheets: the Izar (wrapped round the waist) and the Rida (over the shoulders). Stitched clothes like qamees, shalwar or jubba are not allowed in Ihram for men.
exp.rel: Miqat is the place where pilgrims must enter Ihram. Women wear their normal modest stitched clothes in Ihram.

exp.question: In which year did East Pakistan separate and become Bangladesh?
exp.facts: East Pakistan separated on 16 December 1971 after the war with India and became Bangladesh. 1965 was the Pakistan-India war, 1969 was when Yahya Khan took power, and Pakistan recognised Bangladesh in 1974.
exp.rel: Sheikh Mujib-ur-Rehman was the founder of Bangladesh. The Simla Agreement followed in July 1972.

lc.question: Tarbela Dam is built on the River Indus in which district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
lc.facts: Tarbela Dam is on the River Indus in Haripur District, KP. Swabi lies across the river and Kohat has the small Tanda Dam, while Mansehra has no big dam.
lc.rel: Tarbela is the largest earth-filled dam in the world, completed in 1976. Mangla Dam is on the River Jhelum in Azad Kashmir.

lc.question: Mangla Dam is built on which river? (2)
lc.facts: Mangla Dam is on the River Jhelum in Mirpur, Azad Kashmir. The Indus has Tarbela, the Chenab and Ravi have no big storage dam in Pakistan.
lc.rel: Mangla Dam was completed in 1967. Tarbela Dam is on the River Indus.

lc.question: Which is the largest (longest) river of Pakistan? (2)
lc.facts: The Indus is about 3,180 km long and flows through all of Pakistan to the Arabian Sea. Jhelum, Chenab and Kabul are its smaller tributaries.
lc.rel: The Indus starts in Tibet near Lake Mansarovar. It falls into the Arabian Sea near Thatta, Sindh.

lc.question: Which is the longest river of Asia?
lc.facts: The Yangtze in China is about 6,300 km long, the longest in Asia and third in the world. The Ganges, Indus and Mekong are all much shorter.
lc.rel: The Nile is the longest river in the world. The Three Gorges Dam is on the Yangtze.

lc.question: Which river is commonly called the shortest river of the world?
lc.facts: The Roe River in Montana, USA, is only about 61 m long and is known as the shortest river. The Danube, Thames and Volga are long rivers of Europe.
lc.rel: The Roe River flows into the Missouri River. The Volga is the longest river of Europe.

lc.question: Which is the largest ocean of the world? (2)
lc.facts: The Pacific is the largest ocean, covering about one third of the Earth. The Atlantic is second, the Indian third and the Arctic is the smallest.
lc.rel: The Pacific is also the deepest ocean. The Mariana Trench is in the Pacific.

lc.question: Which is the smallest ocean of the world?
lc.facts: The Arctic Ocean around the North Pole is the smallest and shallowest ocean. The Indian, Southern and Atlantic Oceans are all bigger.
lc.rel: The Pacific is the largest ocean. The Arctic Ocean is covered by ice for most of the year.

lc.question: Which is the deepest ocean of the world?
lc.facts: The Pacific is the deepest ocean; its Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep) is about 11,000 m deep. The Atlantic, Indian and Arctic are shallower.
lc.rel: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is the deepest point on Earth. The Arctic is the shallowest ocean.

lc.question: Which is the smallest country of the world?
lc.facts: Vatican City in Rome is only about 0.44 sq km, the smallest country. Monaco is second smallest, and Nauru and San Marino are bigger.
lc.rel: Vatican City is the home of the Pope. Russia is the largest country by area.

lc.question: Which country has no official capital city?
lc.facts: Nauru, a small island country in the Pacific, has no official capital; government offices are in Yaren District. Tuvalu's capital is Funafuti, the Maldives' is Male, and Monaco is a city-state.
lc.rel: Nauru is the third smallest country by area. Yaren is called its de facto capital.

lc.question: Which country is called the Land of the Rising Sun?
lc.facts: Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun because it is in the far east, where the sun rises first. China, South Korea and Thailand have other titles.
lc.rel: Thailand is called the Land of White Elephants. Norway is called the Land of the Midnight Sun.

lc.question: Which country has the largest number of satellites in space?
lc.facts: The United States has by far the most active satellites, mostly due to SpaceX Starlink. China is second, while Russia and India have far fewer.
lc.rel: The first artificial satellite, Sputnik 1, was launched by the USSR in 1957. Pakistan's first satellite was Badr-1 in 1990.

lc.question: Who is the Chief Minister of Sindh (October 2026)?
lc.facts: Syed Murad Ali Shah of PPP became CM Sindh for a third time in February 2024 and still holds the post. Qaim Ali Shah is a former CM, Sharjeel Memon is a Sindh minister and Kamran Tessori is a former Governor (until March 2026).
lc.rel: Nehal Hashmi (PML-N) has been the Governor of Sindh since 13 March 2026. Karachi is the capital of Sindh.

lc.question: Since 11 October 2026, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has been under Governor's Rule. Who is running the province as Governor?
lc.facts: On 11 October 2026 the President imposed emergency and Governor's Rule in KP, and Governor Faisal Karim Kundi took over the provincial government. Ali Amin Gandapur resigned as CM in October 2025, Sohail Afridi was CM until 11 October 2026, and Haji Ghulam Ali is a former Governor.
lc.rel: Governor's Rule was imposed under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution. Sohail Afridi was CM KP from 15 October 2025 to 11 October 2026.

lc.question: Who is the Chief Minister of Punjab (October 2026)?
lc.facts: Maryam Nawaz Sharif of PML-N became CM Punjab in February 2024 and is the first woman CM of any province. Hamza Shehbaz and Usman Buzdar are former CMs, and Mohsin Naqvi was caretaker CM.
lc.rel: Sardar Saleem Haider Khan is the Governor of Punjab. Lahore is the capital of Punjab.

lc.question: Who is the Chief Minister of Balochistan (October 2026)?
lc.facts: Mir Sarfraz Bugti of PPP was elected CM Balochistan unopposed in March 2024 and still holds the post. Bizenjo and Jam Kamal are former CMs and Ali Mardan Domki was caretaker CM in 2023-24.
lc.rel: Jaffar Khan Mandokhail is the Governor of Balochistan. Quetta is the capital of Balochistan.

lc.question: The Rann of Kutch lies on the border of India and which province of Pakistan?
lc.facts: The Rann of Kutch is a salt marsh between Sindh (Pakistan) and Gujarat (India). Punjab, Balochistan and KP do not touch it.
lc.rel: Pakistan and India fought over the Rann of Kutch in 1965; a tribunal settled it in 1968. Sir Creek is also on the Sindh-Gujarat border.

lc.question: What is the name of the border line between Pakistan and India?
lc.facts: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947 to divide Punjab and Bengal. The Durand Line is the Pak-Afghan border, the McMahon Line is India-China, and the LAC is also India-China.
lc.rel: The Line of Control (LOC) divides Kashmir between Pakistan and India. The Radcliffe Award was announced on 17 August 1947.

lc.question: What is the name of the border line between India and China?
lc.facts: The McMahon Line was drawn in 1914 at the Simla Conference and is the India-China border in the east. The Radcliffe Line is Pak-India, the Durand Line is Pak-Afghan, and the Oder-Neisse Line is Germany-Poland.
lc.rel: The Durand Line was drawn in 1893. The McMahon Line is named after Sir Henry McMahon.

lc.question: What is the name of the border line between Pakistan and Afghanistan?
lc.facts: The Durand Line was drawn in 1893 by Sir Mortimer Durand and is about 2,640 km long. The Radcliffe Line is Pak-India, the McMahon Line is India-China, and the Maginot Line was a French defence line.
lc.rel: The Durand Line agreement was signed with Amir Abdur Rahman Khan. Torkham and Chaman are major crossings on it.

lc.question: What is the real cube root of unity?
lc.facts: The cube roots of unity are 1, omega and omega squared; only 1 is real, because 1 x 1 x 1 = 1. 0 and 2 cubed are not 1, and -1 cubed is -1.
lc.rel: The sum of the three cube roots of unity is 0. Their product is 1.

lc.question: Who wrote the famous book Kitab-ul-Umm?
lc.facts: Kitab-ul-Umm is the main fiqh book of Imam Muhammad bin Idris al-Shafi'i. Imam Malik wrote Al-Muwatta, Imam Ghazali wrote Ihya Ulum al-Din, and Abu Hanifa left no such book.
lc.rel: Imam Shafi'i also wrote Al-Risala on usul al-fiqh. Imam Malik wrote Al-Muwatta.

lc.question: Who wrote Zabur-e-Ajam?
lc.facts: Zabur-e-Ajam (1927) is a Persian poetry book of Allama Muhammad Iqbal. Ghalib, Hali and Faiz wrote other works.
lc.rel: Iqbal's first Urdu book was Bang-e-Dra (1924). His first Persian book was Asrar-e-Khudi (1915).

lc.question: Who wrote Hayat-e-Javed, the biography of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan?
lc.facts: Hayat-e-Javed (1901) is Maulana Altaf Hussain Hali's biography of Sir Syed. Shibli wrote Seerat-un-Nabi, Nazir Ahmad wrote Mirat-ul-Uroos, and Iqbal wrote poetry.
lc.rel: Hali also wrote Musaddas-e-Hali and Yadgar-e-Ghalib. Hayat-e-Saadi is also by Hali.

lc.question: Which country hosted the first Asian Games?
lc.facts: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951. Manila (Philippines) hosted the second in 1954 and Tokyo (Japan) the third in 1958; Pakistan has never hosted them.
lc.rel: The first Asian Games were held in March 1951. The Asian Games are held every four years.

lc.question: In which year were the first Asian Games held?
lc.facts: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in March 1951. 1954 was the second Games in Manila, 1962 was in Jakarta, and 1948 was the London Olympics year.
lc.rel: The idea of the Asian Games was given by Guru Dutt Sondhi of India. The 2026 Asian Games were held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

lc.question: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is in which country?
lc.facts: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is in the city of Pisa, Italy; it is the bell tower of Pisa Cathedral. France, Spain and Greece have other famous landmarks.
lc.rel: The Eiffel Tower is in Paris, France. The Colosseum is in Rome, Italy.

lc.question: Where was Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) born?
lc.facts: The Holy Prophet (SAW) was born in Makkah in 571 CE, the Year of the Elephant. He migrated to Madinah in 622 CE, visited Taif to preach, and Jerusalem is linked to the Miraj.
lc.rel: He was born in Banu Hashim of the Quraysh. He passed away in Madinah in 632 CE.

lc.question: Who looked after Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) in his childhood as his foster mother?
lc.facts: Hazrat Halima Sadia of Banu Saad nursed and raised him in the desert as a child. Hazrat Amina was his own mother, Khadija his first wife and Fatima his daughter.
lc.rel: Hazrat Amina passed away at Abwa when he was six. Umm Ayman (Barakah) also cared for him.

lc.question: Who was the first wife of Hazrat Muhammad (SAW)?
lc.facts: He married Hazrat Khadija (RA) at age 25 when she was 40; she was also the first person to accept Islam. Sauda, Aisha and Hafsa were married later.
lc.rel: Hazrat Khadija passed away in the Year of Sorrow (Aam-ul-Huzn). Hazrat Sauda was his second wife.

lc.question: What is the height of K2, the second highest mountain of the world?
lc.facts: K2 is 8,611 m high and is the highest peak in Pakistan. 8,848 m is Mount Everest, 8,126 m is Nanga Parbat, and 7,708 m is Tirich Mir.
lc.rel: K2 is in the Karakoram Range in Gilgit-Baltistan. It is also called Mount Godwin-Austen.

lc.question: What is another name of K2?
lc.facts: K2 is also called Mount Godwin-Austen, after the British surveyor Henry Godwin-Austen; locally it is Chhogori. Killer Mountain is Nanga Parbat, Everest is in Nepal, and Rakaposhi is another peak.
lc.rel: Nanga Parbat is called the Killer Mountain. K2 is also called the Savage Mountain.

lc.question: What is the value of log 1 (logarithm of unity)?
lc.facts: Log of 1 is 0 in any base, because any base raised to power 0 equals 1. Log 10 to base 10 is 1, and log 0 is undefined.
lc.rel: log of the base itself is 1 (for example log10 of 10 = 1). Log of zero is undefined.

lc.question: In which year was the first countrywide Martial Law imposed in Pakistan?
lc.facts: On 7 October 1958 President Iskander Mirza imposed Martial Law and made General Ayub Khan Chief Martial Law Administrator. 1969 (Yahya Khan) and 1977 (Zia-ul-Haq) were later martial laws, and 1956 was the year of the first Constitution.
lc.rel: Ayub Khan removed Iskander Mirza on 27 October 1958. A limited martial law was imposed in Lahore in 1953.

lc.question: Which is the biggest bird of the world?
lc.facts: The ostrich is the largest and heaviest living bird and cannot fly. The emu is second tallest, and the albatross and condor are big flying birds.
lc.rel: The ostrich also lays the largest egg. The wandering albatross has the largest wingspan.

lc.question: Which is the smallest bird of the world?
lc.facts: The bee hummingbird of Cuba is the smallest bird, about 5 cm long. Sparrows, kiwis and swifts are all much bigger.
lc.rel: Hummingbirds can fly backwards. The ostrich is the largest bird.

lc.question: Which is the fastest bird of the world?
lc.facts: The peregrine falcon dives at over 320 km/h and is the fastest bird (and animal). The ostrich is the fastest runner but cannot fly; the golden eagle is fast but slower; the hummingbird is tiny.
lc.rel: The swift is among the fastest in level flight. The cheetah is the fastest land animal.

lc.question: The kiwi bird is found in which country?
lc.facts: The kiwi is a flightless bird found only in New Zealand and is its national symbol. Australia has the emu, and South Africa and Brazil have no kiwis.
lc.rel: New Zealanders are nicknamed Kiwis. The emu is the national bird of Australia.

lc.question: In which year did the Khilafat Movement start?
lc.facts: The Khilafat Movement was started in 1919 by Indian Muslims, led by the Ali Brothers, to protect the Ottoman Caliphate. 1906 is the founding of the Muslim League, 1916 the Lucknow Pact, and 1924 the end of the Caliphate.
lc.rel: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk abolished the Caliphate in 1924. The Hijrat Movement of 1920 was linked to the Khilafat Movement.

lc.question: In which year was the Deoband Movement (Darul Uloom Deoband) started?
lc.facts: Darul Uloom Deoband was founded on 30 May 1866 by Maulana Qasim Nanotvi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi. 1857 is the War of Independence, 1875 the founding of MAO School Aligarh, and 1885 of the Indian National Congress.
lc.rel: The Nadwat-ul-Ulama was founded in 1894 and later based in Lucknow. Sir Syed founded the MAO School in 1875.

lc.question: When did Gandhi launch the Quit India Movement?
lc.facts: Congress launched the Quit India Movement on 8 August 1942 in Bombay to demand an end to British rule. 23 March 1940 is the Lahore Resolution, 12 March 1930 the start of the Salt March, and 3 June 1947 the partition plan.
lc.rel: Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die' for Quit India. The Cripps Mission came in 1942 too.

lc.question: Who started the Faraizi Movement in Bengal?
lc.facts: Haji Shariatullah started the Faraizi Movement in Bengal in the early 1800s to make Muslims follow the obligatory duties (faraiz). Syed Ahmad Shaheed led the Jihad Movement, Titu Mir fought in Bengal, and Shah Waliullah was an earlier reformer of Delhi.
lc.rel: His son Dudu Mian led the Faraizi Movement after him. Shah Waliullah translated the Quran into Persian.

lc.question: Who started the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930?
lc.facts: Gandhi started the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930 with the Salt March (Dandi March). Nehru and Bose were Congress leaders but did not launch it, and Tilak died in 1920.
lc.rel: The Salt March began on 12 March 1930. The Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931 ended this phase.

lc.question: In which year was the First Round Table Conference held?
lc.facts: The First Round Table Conference was held in London from November 1930 to January 1931; Congress boycotted it. 1931 was the Second and 1932 the Third conference, and 1928 was the Nehru Report.
lc.rel: Quaid-e-Azam attended the First Round Table Conference. Allama Iqbal gave the Allahabad Address in 1930.

lc.question: In which year was the Second Round Table Conference held?
lc.facts: The Second Round Table Conference was held in London in 1931, and Gandhi attended it for Congress. 1930 was the First, 1932 the Third, and 1935 the Government of India Act.
lc.rel: Allama Iqbal attended the Second and Third conferences. The Communal Award came in 1932.

lc.question: In which year was the Third Round Table Conference held?
lc.facts: The Third Round Table Conference was held in London in November-December 1932. 1930 and 1931 were the First and Second, and in 1933 Choudhry Rahmat Ali's pamphlet 'Now or Never' came out.
lc.rel: Congress did not attend the Third conference. Its work led to the Government of India Act 1935.

lc.question: What is the capital of Malaysia?
lc.facts: Kuala Lumpur is the official national capital of Malaysia. Putrajaya is only the administrative centre, Jakarta is the capital of Indonesia, and Singapore is a separate country.
lc.rel: Malaysia's currency is the Ringgit. The Petronas Twin Towers are in Kuala Lumpur.

lc.question: What is the currency of Malaysia?
lc.facts: The Malaysian Ringgit (MYR) is the currency of Malaysia. The Rupiah is Indonesia's, the Baht is Thailand's, and the Peso is the Philippines'.
lc.rel: Kuala Lumpur is the capital of Malaysia. Singapore uses the Singapore Dollar.

lc.question: Which mountain pass connects Pakistan with China?
lc.facts: The Khunjerab Pass (about 4,693 m) in Gilgit-Baltistan links Pakistan and China on the Karakoram Highway. The Khyber Pass leads to Afghanistan, the Bolan Pass is in Balochistan, and the Lowari Pass links Dir and Chitral.
lc.rel: The Karakoram Highway runs through the Khunjerab Pass. The Khyber Pass connects Peshawar with Afghanistan.

lc.question: What is the height of Tirich Mir, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range?
lc.facts: Tirich Mir in Chitral is about 7708 meters high and is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush. 8611 m is K2, 8126 m is Nanga Parbat and 7788 m is Rakaposhi.
lc.rel: Tirich Mir is in Chitral district, KP. K2 (8611 m) is the highest peak in Pakistan.

lc.question: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam present his famous Fourteen Points?
lc.facts: Quaid-e-Azam presented the Fourteen Points in March 1929 (commonly given as 28 March 1929) in reply to the Nehru Report. 1928 was the Nehru Report itself, 1916 the Lucknow Pact and 1930 Allama Iqbal's Allahabad Address.
lc.rel: The Nehru Report came in 1928. Allama Iqbal gave the Allahabad Address in 1930.

lc.question: In which Islamic month is Hajj performed?
lc.facts: Hajj is performed on 8 to 12 Dhul Hijjah, the 12th Islamic month. Ramadan is the month of fasting, Shawwal has Eid ul Fitr and Muharram is the first month of the Islamic year.
lc.rel: Eid ul Adha falls on 10 Dhul Hijjah. The Day of Arafah is 9 Dhul Hijjah.

lc.question: Which mountain range lies in the north-west of Pakistan?
lc.facts: The Hindu Kush lies in the north-west of Pakistan (Chitral area) and its highest peak is Tirich Mir. The Karakoram is in the far north (Gilgit-Baltistan), the Salt Range is in Punjab and the Kirthar Range is in Sindh and Balochistan.
lc.rel: Tirich Mir (7708 m) is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush. K2 is in the Karakoram.

lc.question: Who wrote the book 'Friends Not Masters'?
lc.facts: 'Friends Not Masters' (1967) is the autobiography of President Ayub Khan. Bhutto wrote 'The Myth of Independence', Musharraf wrote 'In the Line of Fire', and Liaquat Ali Khan wrote 'Pakistan: The Heart of Asia'.
lc.rel: Benazir Bhutto wrote 'Daughter of the East'. Ayub Khan ruled from 1958 to 1969.

lc.question: Under the Constitution of Pakistan, the President is the head of:
lc.facts: The President is the Head of State (Article 41) and represents the unity of the Republic. The Prime Minister is the head of government, and Parliament is led by its presiding officers. The President is Supreme Commander, but that is not the main title asked here.
lc.rel: The Prime Minister is the chief executive (head of government). The President is elected by an electoral college.

lc.question: Where is the headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO)?
lc.facts: The WHO headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland. New York has the UN headquarters, Paris has UNESCO and Vienna has the IAEA.
lc.rel: WHO was founded on 7 April 1948, now World Health Day. The WTO and Red Cross (ICRC) are also in Geneva.

lc.question: Warsak Dam is located near which city?
lc.facts: Warsak Dam is on the Kabul River about 30 km from Peshawar, KP. Tarbela is in Haripur, Mangla is near Jhelum (Mirpur), and Kohat has Tanda Dam.
lc.rel: Warsak Dam was completed in the 1960s on the Kabul River. Tanda Dam is in Kohat.

lc.question: Green plants make their food through which process?
lc.facts: Plants make food (glucose) by photosynthesis using sunlight, carbon dioxide and water, with the help of chlorophyll. Respiration breaks food down for energy, transpiration is loss of water from leaves, and digestion happens in animals.
lc.rel: Photosynthesis releases oxygen. Chlorophyll gives plants their green colour.

lc.question: Where is the headquarters of Amnesty International?
lc.facts: Amnesty International has its International Secretariat in London, UK. Geneva has WHO and the Red Cross, New York has the UN, and Paris has UNESCO.
lc.rel: Amnesty International was founded in 1961 in London. It won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.

lc.question: The Indus Waters Treaty between Pakistan and India was brokered by:
lc.facts: The World Bank brokered the Indus Waters Treaty, signed in Karachi in 1960 by Ayub Khan and Nehru. The UN, IMF and ADB were not the mediators.
lc.rel: Pakistan got the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) and India the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej). India announced it was holding the treaty in abeyance in April 2025.

lc.question: Who founded the newspaper Dawn?
lc.facts: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah founded Dawn in Delhi in 1941 as the voice of the Muslim League. Sir Syed started the Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq, and Iqbal and Liaquat Ali Khan did not found Dawn.
lc.rel: Dawn moved to Karachi after 1947. Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar ran 'Comrade' and 'Hamdard'.

lc.question: In which year did World War I start?
lc.facts: World War I started in July 1914 after the killing of Archduke Franz Ferdinand. It ended in 1918, World War II started in 1939, and 1905 was the Partition of Bengal.
lc.rel: World War I ended on 11 November 1918. The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919.

lc.question: In which year was the Kargil War fought?
lc.facts: The Kargil conflict between Pakistan and India was fought in 1999 (May to July). 1965 and 1971 were earlier Pak-India wars, and 1984 was the start of the Siachen conflict.
lc.rel: Captain Karnal Sher Khan and Havaldar Lalak Jan got the Nishan-e-Haider in Kargil. The Lahore Declaration was signed earlier in February 1999.

lc.question: When was the first Cricket World Cup held?
lc.facts: The first Cricket World Cup was held in England in 1975 and the West Indies won it. India won in 1983, Pakistan won in 1992, and 1971 was the first ODI match, not a World Cup.
lc.rel: Pakistan won the 1992 World Cup under Imran Khan. The first ODI was played in 1971 in Melbourne.

lc.question: Who gave the heliocentric (Sun-centred) model of the Solar System?
lc.facts: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed in 1543 that the Sun, not the Earth, is at the centre of the Solar System. Ptolemy gave the Earth-centred model, Galileo later supported Copernicus with his telescope, and Newton gave the laws of gravity.
lc.rel: Copernicus's book was 'De revolutionibus' (1543). Kepler gave the laws of planetary motion.

lc.question: Where is the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
lc.facts: The IMF headquarters is in Washington D.C., USA. New York has the UN, Geneva has WHO, and London has Amnesty International.
lc.rel: The World Bank is also in Washington D.C. Both IMF and World Bank came from the Bretton Woods Conference of 1944.

lc.question: In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed between the Congress and the Muslim League?
lc.facts: The Lucknow Pact was agreed in December 1916 at Lucknow, and Quaid-e-Azam played a key role. 1906 was the founding of the Muslim League, 1919 the Khilafat Movement, and 1920 when Quaid left Congress.
lc.rel: Under the pact Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims. Sarojini Naidu called Jinnah the 'Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity'.

lc.question: When did Quaid-e-Azam resign from the Indian National Congress?
lc.facts: Quaid-e-Azam left Congress in December 1920 (Nagpur session) because he disagreed with Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement. He joined the Muslim League in 1913, 1916 was the Lucknow Pact, and 1928 was the Nehru Report.
lc.rel: Jinnah joined Congress in 1906 and the Muslim League in 1913.

lc.question: World Hepatitis Day is observed on:
lc.facts: World Hepatitis Day is on 28 July, the birthday of Dr Baruch Blumberg who discovered the hepatitis B virus. 7 April is World Health Day, 1 December is World AIDS Day and 24 March is World TB Day.
lc.rel: Hepatitis B and C spread through blood. Hepatitis A and E spread through dirty food and water.

lc.question: What is the approximate range of Pakistan's Nasr (Hatf-IX) missile?
lc.facts: Nasr (Hatf-IX) is a short-range tactical missile with a range of 60 km, raised to 70 km in the improved version (2017). 290 km is Ghaznavi, 750 km is Shaheen-I and 2750 km is Shaheen-III.
lc.rel: Ababeel (MIRV) has a range of about 2200 km. Babur is a cruise missile.

lc.question: In which year was the Pakistan-China boundary agreement signed?
lc.facts: Pakistan and China signed their boundary agreement on 2 March 1963. 1951 is when diplomatic ties began, and 1978 is when the Karakoram Highway opened.
lc.rel: Khunjerab Pass is on the Pak-China border. Diplomatic relations started on 21 May 1951.

lc.question: The 38th parallel divides which two countries?
lc.facts: The 38th parallel is the line that divides North Korea and South Korea. The McMahon Line is between India and China, the 17th parallel divided Vietnam, and the 49th parallel is the USA-Canada border.
lc.rel: The Korean War was fought from 1950 to 1953. The Radcliffe Line is the Pak-India border.

lc.question: Who was the first President of Pakistan?
lc.facts: Iskander Mirza became the first President in March 1956 under the 1956 Constitution. Ghulam Muhammad was Governor-General, Ayub Khan was the second President, and Fazal Ilahi Chaudhry was President under the 1973 Constitution.
lc.rel: Iskander Mirza imposed the first Martial Law on 7 October 1958. Quaid-e-Azam was the first Governor-General.

lc.question: In which year did Malala Yousafzai win the Nobel Peace Prize?
lc.facts: Malala won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, sharing it with Kailash Satyarthi of India. 2012 was the year she was attacked, and 2013 and 2016 are wrong.
lc.rel: She is the youngest Nobel laureate (age 17). Dr Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979.

lc.question: Who is the President of China (October 2026)?
lc.facts: Xi Jinping has been President of China since 2013 and still holds the post. Li Qiang is the Premier, Wang Yi is the Foreign Minister, and Hu Jintao was the earlier President.
lc.rel: Xi Jinping is also General Secretary of the Communist Party. Li Qiang became Premier in 2023.

lc.question: Muhammad bin Qasim invaded Sindh in:
lc.facts: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 712 CE and defeated Raja Dahir. 1001 CE was Mahmud of Ghazni's first attack, 1192 CE was the Second Battle of Tarain, and 632 CE was when the Prophet (PBUH) passed away.
lc.rel: Sindh is called 'Bab-ul-Islam' (Gateway of Islam). He was sent by Hajjaj bin Yusuf.

lc.question: In which year did Pakistan buy Gwadar from Oman?
lc.facts: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultanate of Oman in 1958 (handed over on 8 September 1958) during Feroz Khan Noon's government. The other years are wrong.
lc.rel: Gwadar is in Balochistan on the Arabian Sea. It is a key port of CPEC.

lc.question: How many seats are reserved for women in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
lc.facts: Article 51 reserves 60 seats for women in the National Assembly, and this is still the number in 2026. 10 seats are for non-Muslims, 70 is wrong, and 33 is not the women quota in the NA.
lc.rel: The National Assembly has 336 seats: 266 general, 60 women and 10 minorities. Women's seats were raised to 60 in 2002.

lc.question: Which is the largest desert of Pakistan?
lc.facts: The Thar Desert (in Sindh and part of Punjab) is the largest desert in Pakistan. Thal is in Punjab, Kharan is in Balochistan, and Cholistan is a smaller desert in Punjab next to Thar.
lc.rel: Thar is also called the Great Indian Desert. Thar coal is in Sindh.

lc.question: What is the reported range of Pakistan's Ababeel missile?
lc.facts: Ababeel is a MIRV ballistic missile with a reported range of about 2200 km, first tested in 2017. 70 km is Nasr, 750 km is Shaheen-I and 2750 km is Shaheen-III.
lc.rel: MIRV means one missile can carry several warheads. Shaheen-III (2750 km) is Pakistan's longest-range tested missile.

lc.question: For how many days was the 1965 Pakistan-India war fought?
lc.facts: The 1965 war lasted 17 days, from 6 September to 23 September 1965. The 1971 war lasted about 13 days, and 30 and 7 days are wrong.
lc.rel: 6 September is Defence Day in Pakistan. The Tashkent Declaration was signed in January 1966.

lc.question: In which year was the present Constitution of Pakistan adopted?
lc.facts: The present Constitution was passed on 10 April 1973 and came into force on 14 August 1973. 1956 and 1962 were earlier constitutions, and 1985 was the 8th Amendment.
lc.rel: 1956 was the first Constitution. 1962 was the second, under Ayub Khan.

lc.question: Which river is generally called the longest river in the world?
lc.facts: The Nile in Africa (about 6650 km) is usually counted as the longest river. The Amazon carries the most water, the Yangtze is the longest in Asia, and the Indus is the longest in Pakistan.
lc.rel: The Yangtze is Asia's longest river. The Indus is Pakistan's largest river.

lc.question: Who wrote 'Mein Kampf'?
lc.facts: Adolf Hitler wrote 'Mein Kampf' (My Struggle) in the 1920s. Marx wrote 'Das Kapital', and Mussolini and Stalin did not write it.
lc.rel: Hitler led Nazi Germany in World War II. Karl Marx also wrote 'The Communist Manifesto'.

lc.question: In which year was the Lahore Declaration signed between Pakistan and India?
lc.facts: The Lahore Declaration was signed in February 1999 by Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee. 1966 was Tashkent, 1972 was the Simla Agreement, and 2004 was the Islamabad meeting.
lc.rel: Vajpayee came to Lahore by bus. The Kargil War came later the same year.

lc.question: About what percentage of the adult human body is water?
lc.facts: Water makes up about 50-60% of an adult body weight (about 60% in men). 20-30% and 10-15% are too low, and 80-90% is too high for a whole adult.
lc.rel: Blood plasma is about 90% water. Babies have about 75% water.

lc.question: Islam originated in the:
lc.facts: Islam began in Makkah, in the Arabian Peninsula, in the 7th century. Persia, Egypt and Central Asia received Islam later through conquest and preaching.
lc.rel: The first revelation came in Cave Hira in 610 CE. Makkah and Madinah are in today's Saudi Arabia.

lc.question: What is the value of cos 0 degrees?
lc.facts: cos 0 degrees = 1. sin 0 degrees is 0, tan 90 degrees is undefined, and cos 180 degrees is -1.
lc.rel: sin 90 degrees = 1. cos 90 degrees = 0.

lc.question: Which country is called the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes'?
lc.facts: Finland is called the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes' (it really has about 188,000 lakes). Norway is the Land of the Midnight Sun, Switzerland is the Playground of Europe, and Canada is the Land of Maple Leaf.
lc.rel: Japan is the Land of the Rising Sun. Helsinki is the capital of Finland.

lc.question: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
lc.facts: Astana is the capital of Kazakhstan. It was called Nur-Sultan from 2019 to 2022 and then renamed Astana again. Almaty was the old capital, Tashkent is in Uzbekistan and Bishkek is in Kyrgyzstan.
lc.rel: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world. Its currency is the tenge.

lc.question: Which disease is caused by the bite of an infected dog?
lc.facts: Rabies is a virus spread by the bite of an infected dog (or other animal). Malaria comes from mosquitoes, typhoid from dirty food and water, and tetanus from a bacterium in soil and rusty wounds.
lc.rel: Louis Pasteur made the rabies vaccine in 1885. Rabies is also called hydrophobia (fear of water).

lc.question: The Hingol River flows in which province of Pakistan?
lc.facts: The Hingol River is in Balochistan and is the longest river of Balochistan. It flows through Hingol National Park into the Arabian Sea. It is not in Sindh, KP or Punjab.
lc.rel: Hingol National Park is the largest national park in Pakistan. The Hinglaj temple is near the river.

lc.question: In English grammar, 'the' is:
lc.facts: 'The' is the definite article because it points to a specific thing. 'A' and 'an' are indefinite articles, and 'the' is not a pronoun or preposition.
lc.rel: Use 'an' before a vowel sound (an hour). Use 'a' before a consonant sound (a university).

lc.question: The Battle of Plassey was fought on:
lc.facts: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757, when Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah. 1764 was the Battle of Buxar, 1799 was Tipu Sultan's death, and 1857 was the War of Independence.
lc.rel: Mir Jafar betrayed Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey. The Battle of Buxar (1764) made the British stronger in Bengal.

lc.question: World War II ended on:
lc.facts: World War II formally ended on 2 September 1945, when Japan signed the surrender. 1 September 1939 is when it started, 11 November 1918 ended World War I, and the war in Europe ended on 8 May 1945, not 1944.
lc.rel: Atomic bombs hit Hiroshima (6 August 1945) and Nagasaki (9 August 1945). The UN was founded on 24 October 1945.

lc.question: The Al-Khalid main battle tank was inducted into the Pakistan Army in which decade?
lc.facts: Al-Khalid was made by Heavy Industries Taxila with China and was inducted into the Pakistan Army in 2001, so in the 2000s. It was being developed in the 1990s but not yet inducted, and the 1970s and 1980s are too early.
lc.rel: Al-Khalid is made at Heavy Industries Taxila (HIT). It was based on Chinese tank designs.

lc.question: Choose the antonym of 'Embrace':
lc.facts: 'Embrace' means to accept or hold warmly, so its opposite is 'reject'. Hug, accept and adopt are close in meaning (synonyms), not opposites.
lc.rel: Synonyms of embrace: welcome, accept. Antonyms: refuse, spurn.

lc.question: Milk is boiled mainly to:
lc.facts: Boiling milk kills harmful bacteria and pathogens so it is safe to drink. Boiling does not add vitamins (it can reduce some), does not increase fat and does not make milk sweeter.
lc.rel: Pasteurisation (Louis Pasteur) heats milk to kill germs. Curd is made by Lactobacillus bacteria.

seerah.question: In which year was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) born in Makkah?
seerah.facts: He was born in Makkah in 571 CE (some books say 570 CE), in the Year of the Elephant. 610 CE is the year of the first revelation and 632 CE is the year he passed away. 550 CE is too early.
seerah.rel: He was born on 12 Rabi ul Awwal (common view) in the Year of the Elephant (Aam al-Feel). First revelation came in 610 CE at age 40.

seerah.question: To which clan of the Quraysh tribe did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) belong?
seerah.facts: He belonged to Banu Hashim, the clan named after his great-grandfather Hashim. Banu Makhzum was the clan of Abu Jahl and Khalid bin Walid, Banu Umayyah of Abu Sufyan and Uthman (RA), and Banu Taym of Abu Bakr (RA).
seerah.rel: Hashim was the great-grandfather of the Prophet (PBUH). Banu Hashim were boycotted in Shib Abi Talib for about 3 years.

seerah.question: What was the name of Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) mother?
seerah.facts: His mother was Aminah bint Wahb from Banu Zuhrah. Halimah was his foster (wet) mother, Fatimah was his daughter, and Safiyyah was his aunt (and also the name of a wife).
seerah.rel: Aminah died at Abwa, between Makkah and Madinah. Her father Wahb was chief of Banu Zuhrah.

seerah.question: Who was the father of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
seerah.facts: His father was Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib, who died before the Prophet (PBUH) was born. Abdul Muttalib was his grandfather, and Abu Talib and Hamza were his uncles.
seerah.rel: Abdullah died in Yathrib (Madinah) on the way back from a trade journey to Syria.

seerah.question: Who was the foster mother who nursed Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in the desert?
seerah.facts: Halimah al-Sa'diyyah of Banu Sa'd nursed him in the desert. Umm Ayman (Barakah) was his nurse/caretaker in Makkah, Fatimah bint Asad was Abu Talib's wife, and Sobia is a wrong option.
seerah.rel: Thuwaybah, a freed slave of Abu Lahab, also nursed him for a few days. The event of opening of the chest (Shaq-e-Sadr) happened while he was with Halimah.

seerah.question: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when his mother passed away?
seerah.facts: His mother Aminah died when he was 6 years old, at Abwa. He was 8 when his grandfather died and about 12 on the Syria journey, so those ages are for other events.
seerah.rel: Umm Ayman brought him back to Makkah after his mother's death.

seerah.question: Who took care of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) after his mother's death?
seerah.facts: His grandfather Abdul Muttalib took care of him after his mother died. Abu Talib took care of him later, after Abdul Muttalib died. Abu Lahab was an enemy, and Hamza was a young uncle.
seerah.rel: Abdul Muttalib looked after him for about 2 years, until the Prophet (PBUH) was 8.

seerah.question: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when his grandfather Abdul Muttalib died?
seerah.facts: Abdul Muttalib died when the Prophet (PBUH) was 8 years old. He was 6 when his mother died and about 12 on the Syria trip, so the other options are wrong.
seerah.rel: After Abdul Muttalib, his uncle Abu Talib became his guardian.

seerah.question: Which uncle took responsibility for Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) after his grandfather's death?
seerah.facts: Abu Talib, the full brother of his father Abdullah, became his guardian. Abu Lahab opposed Islam, while Abbas and Hamza did not raise him.
seerah.rel: Abu Talib protected him until his own death in the Year of Sorrow (10th year of Prophethood). Abu Talib was the father of Ali (RA).

seerah.question: Who accompanied Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) on the journey to Syria during his childhood?
seerah.facts: He went to Syria with his uncle Abu Talib on a trade caravan when he was about 12. Abdul Muttalib had already died, and Abu Bakr and Hamza did not go on this trip.
seerah.rel: On this trip the Christian monk Bahira recognised signs of prophethood in him at Busra. His second Syria trip was for Khadijah (RA) with her servant Maysarah.

seerah.question: Which titles were associated with Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) because of his honesty?
seerah.facts: The people of Makkah called him Al-Amin (the trustworthy) and As-Sadiq (the truthful). Al-Farooq is the title of Umar (RA), As-Siddiq of Abu Bakr (RA), and Saifullah of Khalid bin Walid (RA).
seerah.rel: Because he was Al-Amin, the Quraysh accepted his decision on placing the Black Stone (Hajr-e-Aswad) in the Kaaba.

seerah.question: Which pact did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) participate in to support the oppressed?
seerah.facts: Hilf al-Fudul was a pact made in Makkah before prophethood to help the oppressed, and he took part in it as a young man. Hudaybiyyah (6 AH), the Pledges of Aqabah and the Charter of Madinah all came after prophethood.
seerah.rel: Hilf al-Fudul was made in the house of Abdullah ibn Jud'an after the Harb al-Fijar wars.

seerah.question: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when he married Hazrat Khadijah (RA)?
seerah.facts: He married Khadijah (RA) at the age of 25, and she was about 40. 40 was his age at the first revelation, so the other options are wrong.
seerah.rel: Khadijah (RA) was his first wife, and he did not marry anyone else during her life. All his children except Ibrahim were from her.

seerah.question: Which Surah contains the first five verses identified as the first revelation?
seerah.facts: The first revelation was the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq, starting with Iqra (Read), in the Cave of Hira. Al-Muddaththir came after the pause in revelation, and Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah came later.
seerah.rel: Surah Al-Alaq is the 96th Surah. The first complete Surah revealed is commonly said to be Al-Fatihah.

seerah.question: Who was the first person to accept Islam?
seerah.facts: Hazrat Khadijah (RA) was the first person of all to accept Islam. Abu Bakr (RA) was the first free adult man, Ali (RA) the first child, and Zayd (RA) the first freed slave.
seerah.rel: Khadijah (RA) died in the Year of Sorrow, the same year as Abu Talib.

seerah.question: Who is commonly identified as the first adult free man to accept Islam?
seerah.facts: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA) was the first free adult man to accept Islam. Ali (RA) was a child then, Uthman (RA) accepted Islam through Abu Bakr (RA), and Umar (RA) accepted Islam years later.
seerah.rel: Through Abu Bakr (RA), Uthman, Zubair, Talha, Abdur Rahman bin Auf and Saad bin Abi Waqqas (RA) accepted Islam.

seerah.question: Who is commonly identified as the first child to accept Islam?
seerah.facts: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) was about 10 years old when he accepted Islam, so he was the first child Muslim. Hasan, Husayn and Usama (RA) were born after that.
seerah.rel: Ali (RA) lived in the Prophet's (PBUH) house as a child. He later married Fatimah (RA).

seerah.question: Who was the first freed slave commonly identified among the earliest Muslims?
seerah.facts: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA), the freed slave and adopted son of the Prophet (PBUH), was among the first four Muslims. Bilal (RA) accepted Islam a little later, Ammar (RA) was not a freed slave of the Prophet, and Salman (RA) accepted Islam in Madinah.
seerah.rel: Zayd (RA) is the only companion named in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab). He was martyred at the Battle of Mu'tah.

seerah.question: For approximately how many years was the Islamic message initially preached privately?
seerah.facts: The secret preaching lasted about 3 years. Then Allah ordered open preaching, and the Prophet (PBUH) called the Quraysh from Mount Safa. 2, 5 and 7 years are not the accepted period.
seerah.rel: Dar al-Arqam was the house used as the secret centre of the early Muslims.

seerah.question: Which Christian scholar did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) meet through Hazrat Khadijah (RA)?
seerah.facts: After the first revelation, Khadijah (RA) took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, who said the same angel (Namus) came to Musa (AS). Bahira was the monk met on the Syria trip, Heraclius was the Roman emperor, and Nestorius was an old church leader.
seerah.rel: Waraqah was Khadijah's (RA) cousin and knew the Torah and Gospel.

seerah.question: From which hill did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) publicly call the Quraysh to Islam?
seerah.facts: He stood on Mount Safa near the Kaaba and called the Quraysh openly to Islam. Uhud is in Madinah, Arafat is outside Makkah, and Marwah is the other hill of Sa'i, not this event.
seerah.rel: Before that he invited his family to a dinner (Dawat-e-Dhul Ashira).

seerah.question: Which uncle opposed Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during his public warning at Mount Safa?
seerah.facts: Abu Lahab cursed him at Mount Safa, and Surah Al-Lahab (Al-Masad) was revealed about him. Abu Talib protected him, Hamza later accepted Islam, and Abbas did not oppose him there.
seerah.rel: Abu Lahab's real name was Abdul Uzza. His wife Umm Jamil is also condemned in the same Surah.

seerah.question: Who is traditionally recognized as the first martyr of Islam?
seerah.facts: Sumayyah (RA), mother of Ammar (RA), was killed by Abu Jahl and is the first martyr of Islam. Her husband Yasir (RA) was also martyred but after her, Bilal (RA) survived, and Hamza (RA) was martyred later at Uhud.
seerah.rel: The first male martyr is commonly said to be Yasir (RA). Hamza (RA) is called Sayyid ush-Shuhada (leader of martyrs).

seerah.question: Which companion endured persecution while repeatedly declaring the oneness of Allah?
seerah.facts: Bilal (RA) was tortured by his master Umayyah ibn Khalaf on hot sand but kept saying Ahad, Ahad (Allah is One). Ammar, Abu Dharr and Khabbab (RA) were also persecuted, but the Ahad Ahad story is of Bilal (RA).
seerah.rel: Abu Bakr (RA) bought Bilal (RA) and set him free. Bilal (RA) later became the first Mu'adhdhin of Islam.

seerah.question: Where did the first migration of Muslims to escape persecution take place?
seerah.facts: The first Hijrah was to Abyssinia (Habshah, now Ethiopia) in the 5th year of Prophethood. Hijrah to Yathrib (Madinah) was later, Taif was only a visit, and Yemen is wrong.
seerah.rel: Uthman (RA) and his wife Ruqayyah (RA) were in the first group. Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (RA) spoke before the Najashi in the second migration.

seerah.question: What title was used for the Christian ruler of Abyssinia who gave shelter to Muslims?
seerah.facts: The king of Abyssinia was called Najashi (Negus); his name was Ashama. Heraclius was the Roman emperor, Chosroes (Kisra) the Persian king, and Muqawqis the ruler of Egypt.
seerah.rel: Najashi Ashama later accepted Islam, and the Prophet (PBUH) offered his funeral prayer in absentia.

seerah.question: Which uncle and protector of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) died during the Year of Sorrow?
seerah.facts: Abu Talib died in the 10th year of Prophethood, called Aam al-Huzn (Year of Sorrow). Abu Lahab died after Badr, Hamza (RA) was martyred at Uhud, and Abbas (RA) lived long after.
seerah.rel: Khadijah (RA) also died in the Year of Sorrow.

seerah.question: Which city did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) visit seeking support after facing opposition in Makkah?
seerah.facts: After the Year of Sorrow he went to Taif to seek help, but its people stoned him. Madinah was the place of Hijrah later, and Khaybar and Tabuk are places of later expeditions.
seerah.rel: Taif is the city of the Banu Thaqif tribe. On the way back, a Christian slave named Addas met him.

seerah.question: Which companion accompanied Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) on his journey to Taif?
seerah.facts: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) went with him to Taif and was injured while protecting him. Abu Bakr (RA) was his companion in the Hijrah, not Taif; Ali and Umar (RA) did not go.
seerah.rel: The Taif journey was in the 10th year of Prophethood.

seerah.question: What is the night journey from Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa called?
seerah.facts: The night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem is called Isra. Mi'raj is the ascension from Al-Aqsa to the heavens, Hijrah is migration, and Ghazwah is a battle.
seerah.rel: Surah Bani Israel (Al-Isra) begins with this journey. The Prophet (PBUH) rode Buraq.

seerah.question: What is the ascension of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to the heavens called?
seerah.facts: Mi'raj means the ascension from Masjid al-Aqsa up through the heavens. Isra is only the night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem. Ghazwah is a battle and Umrah is the lesser pilgrimage.
seerah.rel: Isra and Mi'raj happened about one year before Hijrah. Surah Bani Israil (Al-Isra) starts with the Isra.

seerah.question: Which fundamental act of worship was prescribed during the event of Mi'raj?
seerah.facts: The five daily prayers (Salah) were made obligatory on the night of Mi'raj. Fasting and Zakat came in 2 AH in Madinah, and Hajj was made obligatory later (about 9 AH).
seerah.rel: At first 50 prayers were ordered, then reduced to 5 with the reward of 50. Salah is the only worship made obligatory in the heavens.

seerah.question: From which sacred mosque did the night journey begin in Makkah?
seerah.facts: The Isra began at Masjid al-Haram in Makkah, as Surah Al-Isra verse 1 says. Masjid al-Aqsa was the end point of the journey. Quba and Masjid an-Nabawi are in Madinah and were built after Hijrah.
seerah.rel: Isra: Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa on the Buraq. Masjid al-Aqsa was the first Qiblah.

seerah.question: What were the pledges made between Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and people from Yathrib called?
seerah.facts: The people of Yathrib gave their pledges at Aqabah near Mina, so they are called the Pledges of Aqabah. Hudaybiyyah (6 AH) was a treaty with Quraysh, the Charter of Madinah came after Hijrah, and Ridwan was under a tree at Hudaybiyyah.
seerah.rel: First Aqabah: 12 men (621 CE). Second Aqabah: about 73 men and 2 women (622 CE).

seerah.question: What was the earlier name of Madinah?
seerah.facts: Madinah was called Yathrib before Hijrah; it became Madinat-un-Nabi, the City of the Prophet. Bakkah is an old name of Makkah, Faran is a name linked to the Makkah area, and Khaybar is a separate oasis north of Madinah.
seerah.rel: Madinah is also called Taybah. Makkah is also called Umm al-Qura.

seerah.question: Who was sent to Yathrib as an early Muslim teacher after the First Pledge of Aqabah?
seerah.facts: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) was the first teacher (envoy) of Islam sent to Yathrib. Abu Bakr and Bilal stayed in Makkah, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal was a man of Madinah, later sent to Yemen.
seerah.rel: Mus'ab ibn Umayr was the standard-bearer martyred at Uhud. Mu'adh ibn Jabal was sent to Yemen as governor and teacher.

seerah.question: Who slept in Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) bed on the night of Hijrah?
seerah.facts: Ali (RA) slept in the Prophet's bed to trick the Quraysh and later returned people's trusts (amanat). Abu Bakr travelled with the Prophet, Umar had migrated openly earlier, and Uthman had gone to Abyssinia and Madinah.
seerah.rel: Hijrah took place in 622 CE (Rabi al-Awwal, 1 AH era). Ali joined the Prophet in Quba a few days later.

seerah.question: Who accompanied Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during the migration to Madinah?
seerah.facts: Abu Bakr (RA) was the Prophet's companion on the Hijrah and in the cave (Surah At-Tawbah 9:40). Ali stayed back in Makkah, Umar migrated before, and Zayd went with the Prophet to Taif, not on Hijrah.
seerah.rel: Abdullah ibn Urayqit was their guide. Asma bint Abi Bakr brought food and got the title Dhat an-Nitaqayn.

seerah.question: In which cave did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Abu Bakr (RA) take refuge during Hijrah?
seerah.facts: They hid for three nights in the Cave of Thawr, south of Makkah. Cave Hira is where the first revelation came, and Uhud and Quba are places in Madinah.
seerah.rel: Cave Hira is on Jabal an-Nur. The spider web and the dove's nest at Thawr are famous stories.

seerah.question: Who was the leader of the hypocrites in Madinah commonly mentioned in Seerah?
seerah.facts: Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul led the hypocrites (Munafiqun) in Madinah. Abu Jahl was an open enemy in Makkah, Musaylimah was a false prophet, and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf was a Jewish poet.
seerah.rel: Ibn Ubayy went back with about 300 men before Uhud. Surah Al-Munafiqun is about the hypocrites.

seerah.question: Which Jewish scholar of Madinah accepted Islam and became a companion?
seerah.facts: Abdullah ibn Salam (RA), a rabbi of Banu Qaynuqa, accepted Islam soon after Hijrah. Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Huyayy ibn Akhtab stayed enemies, and Abu Jahl was a pagan of Makkah.
seerah.rel: Huyayy ibn Akhtab was a chief of Banu Nadir. Safiyyah (RA), his daughter, became a wife of the Prophet.

seerah.question: What title was given to the Muslims of Madinah who welcomed the emigrants?
seerah.facts: Ansar means helpers; they were the Muslims of Madinah (Aws and Khazraj). Muhajirun were the emigrants from Makkah, Tabi'un came after the companions, and Ashab al-Suffah lived on the Suffah platform.
seerah.rel: The Ansar came from two tribes: Aws and Khazraj. The Prophet made brotherhood (Mu'akhat) between Ansar and Muhajirun.

seerah.question: What was the platform in Masjid an-Nabawi associated with companions devoted to learning?
seerah.facts: The Suffah was a shaded platform where poor companions lived and learned; it is called the first residential school of Islam. The Mihrab is the prayer niche, the Minbar is the pulpit, and the Rawdah is the area between the pulpit and the Prophet's house.
seerah.rel: Abu Hurairah (RA) was one of the famous Ashab al-Suffah. Masjid an-Nabawi was built in 1 AH.

seerah.question: Which companion reported a dream containing the wording of the Adhan?
seerah.facts: Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA) saw the words of the Adhan in a dream and told the Prophet, who approved them. Bilal was told to call it because of his strong voice. Uthman and Abu Bakr did not report this dream.
seerah.rel: The Adhan began in 1 AH (some say 2 AH) in Madinah. Bilal (RA) was the first Mu'adhdhin.

seerah.question: Who became the most famous early Mu'adhdhin of Islam?
seerah.facts: Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) was the first and most famous Mu'adhdhin of the Prophet. Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum was a second Mu'adhdhin but less famous, while Ammar and Salman were not Mu'adhdhins.
seerah.rel: Bilal gave the Adhan on the Kaaba at the Conquest of Makkah (8 AH). His former master was Umayyah ibn Khalaf.

seerah.question: In which month of 2 AH was fasting in Ramadan made obligatory?
seerah.facts: The order to fast in Ramadan came in Sha'ban of 2 AH, just before the first Ramadan in Madinah. Ramadan is the month of fasting itself, not the month the order came, and Rajab and Shawwal are wrong months.
seerah.rel: The Qiblah was also changed in 2 AH (Rajab or Sha'ban). Battle of Badr was on 17 Ramadan 2 AH.

seerah.question: In which year of Hijrah was the obligation of Ramadan fasting introduced?
seerah.facts: Fasting in Ramadan became obligatory in 2 AH. In 1 AH Masjid an-Nabawi was built, 5 AH was the Battle of the Trench, and 9 AH is when Hajj became obligatory (per most scholars).
seerah.rel: Zakat and Eid prayers also started in 2 AH. Surah Al-Baqarah 2:183 is the fasting verse.

seerah.question: In which direction did Muslims pray before the Qiblah was changed to the Kaaba?
seerah.facts: Muslims first prayed toward Bait al-Maqdis (Masjid al-Aqsa) in Jerusalem for about 16-17 months after Hijrah. Damascus, Cairo and Mount Sinai were never the Qiblah.
seerah.rel: The Qiblah changed to the Kaaba in 2 AH (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:144). Masjid al-Aqsa is called the first Qiblah.

seerah.question: Which mosque is associated with the change of Qiblah during prayer?
seerah.facts: Masjid al-Qiblatayn means the mosque of two Qiblahs, because the Qiblah changed during a prayer there. Quba is the first mosque built in Islam, Masjid an-Nabawi is the Prophet's mosque, and al-Ghamamah is linked to Eid prayer.
seerah.rel: Masjid Quba is the first mosque of Islam. The Qiblah change came in 2 AH.

seerah.question: Which daughter of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) married Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)?
seerah.facts: Fatimah (RA) married Ali (RA) in 2 AH. Zaynab married Abu al-As, and Ruqayyah and then Umm Kulthum married Uthman (RA).
seerah.rel: Uthman (RA) is called Dhun-Nurayn because he married two daughters of the Prophet. Hasan and Husayn were sons of Ali and Fatimah.

seerah.question: Which expedition is regarded as the first Ghazwah led personally by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
seerah.facts: Ghazwah al-Abwa (Waddan), in Safar 2 AH, was the first expedition the Prophet led himself. Buwat, Safwan (first Badr) and Ushayrah came after it in the same year.
seerah.rel: Ushayrah led to a treaty with Banu Mudlij. Badr al-Kubra (17 Ramadan 2 AH) was the first big battle.

seerah.question: What is a military campaign attended personally by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) called?
seerah.facts: A Ghazwah is a campaign in which the Prophet himself took part. A Sariyyah is one he sent without going himself, Hijrah is migration, and Umrah is the lesser pilgrimage.
seerah.rel: Most counts give 27 Ghazwat and about 50 or more Saraya. The last Ghazwah was Tabuk (9 AH).

seerah.question: Which prominent Quraysh leader was killed at Badr?
seerah.facts: Abu Jahl (Amr ibn Hisham) was killed at Badr by the young Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh, and finished by Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah and Amr ibn al-Aas survived and later accepted Islam.
seerah.rel: Abu Jahl was called the Pharaoh of this Ummah. Abu Sufyan led the Quraysh caravan before Badr.

seerah.question: How many Muslims were martyred at the Battle of Badr according to accounts?
seerah.facts: 14 Muslims were martyred at Badr (6 Muhajirun and 8 Ansar). 70 is the number of Quraysh killed at Badr and also of Muslims martyred at Uhud, so it is wrong here.
seerah.rel: 313 Muslims fought about 1,000 Quraysh at Badr. 70 Quraysh were killed and 70 captured.

seerah.question: Approximately how many Quraysh fighters were killed at Badr?
seerah.facts: About 70 Quraysh were killed and about 70 were taken prisoner at Badr. 14 is the number of Muslim martyrs, and 100 and 300 are not given in the accounts.
seerah.rel: Badr was on 17 Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE). The Muslims were 313 against about 1,000.

seerah.question: Which daughter of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) died around the time of the Battle of Badr?
seerah.facts: Ruqayyah (RA), wife of Uthman, died in Madinah while the Muslims were at Badr; Uthman stayed back to nurse her. Zaynab died in 8 AH, Umm Kulthum in 9 AH, and Fatimah after the Prophet.
seerah.rel: Uthman then married Umm Kulthum and got the title Dhun-Nurayn. Uthman got a share of Badr booty though absent.

seerah.question: What educational condition was set for releasing certain literate prisoners after Badr?
options: Teach children to read and write
seerah.facts: Literate prisoners who could not pay ransom were freed after each taught 10 Muslim children to read and write. Ransom was for those who could pay, no one was forced to convert, and building houses was not a condition.
seerah.rel: Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) learned writing this way. Ransom per prisoner was about 1,000 to 4,000 dirhams.

seerah.question: What name does the Qur'an use for the day of the Battle of Badr?
seerah.facts: Surah Al-Anfal 8:41 calls Badr Yaum al-Furqan, the Day of Criterion between truth and falsehood. Fath refers to the Conquest of Makkah, Ahzab to the Trench, and Jumu'ah is Friday.
seerah.rel: Surah Al-Anfal was revealed about Badr. Surah Al-Ahzab is about the Battle of the Trench (5 AH).

seerah.question: According to the Qur'an, how many angels were initially promised as reinforcement at Badr?
seerah.facts: Surah Al-Anfal 8:9 says Allah helped with a thousand angels one after another. 3,000 and 5,000 are mentioned in Surah Al-Imran as further promises, and 100 and 10,000 are not mentioned.
seerah.rel: Surah Al-Imran 3:124-125 mentions 3,000 and 5,000 angels. 10,000 was the size of the Muslim army at the Conquest of Makkah.

seerah.question: Who was the former master of Bilal (RA) who was killed at Badr?
seerah.facts: Umayyah ibn Khalaf tortured Bilal (RA) in Makkah and was killed at Badr. Utbah and Walid were killed in the first duels at Badr but were not Bilal's masters, and Abu Lahab did not go to Badr and died in Makkah.
seerah.rel: Abu Bakr (RA) bought and freed Bilal. Hamza, Ali and Ubaydah fought the first duels at Badr.

seerah.question: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was captured at Badr?
seerah.facts: Abbas (RA) fought on the Quraysh side and was taken prisoner, then paid ransom. Abu Talib had died before Hijrah, Hamza fought for the Muslims, and Abu Lahab did not join the battle.
seerah.rel: Abbas openly accepted Islam before the Conquest of Makkah. Abu Lahab died a few days after Badr.

seerah.question: Which Jewish tribe was expelled from Madinah after the conflict following Badr?
seerah.facts: Banu Qaynuqa broke the treaty after Badr and were expelled in 2 AH. Banu Nadir were expelled in 4 AH, Banu Qurayzah were punished after the Trench in 5 AH, and Ghatafan was an Arab tribe, not Jewish.
seerah.rel: The three Jewish tribes of Madinah: Qaynuqa, Nadir, Qurayzah. Surah Al-Hashr is about Banu Nadir.

seerah.question: Which cousin of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) distinguished himself in the fighting at Badr?
seerah.facts: Ali (RA), the Prophet's cousin, won his duel against Walid ibn Utbah and fought bravely at Badr. Abu Bakr was not a cousin and stayed with the Prophet at the command shelter, Uthman was absent, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal was not a cousin.
seerah.rel: Ali got the sword Dhul-Fiqar at Badr. Hamza (RA) killed Utbah ibn Rabi'ah in the duels.

seerah.question: Which Surah contains the final explicit Qur'anic prohibition of intoxicants?
seerah.facts: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:90-91 gave the final, complete ban on wine and gambling. Al-Baqarah 2:219 only said the harm is greater than the benefit, while Al-Fil and Al-Kawthar are short Makki surahs not about intoxicants.
seerah.rel: Wine was banned in stages: Al-Baqarah 2:219, An-Nisa 4:43, then Al-Ma'idah 5:90. The final ban came around 3-4 AH.

seerah.question: Which expedition is commonly known as the Battle of Sawiq?
seerah.facts: Ghazwah as-Sawiq (2 AH) was the chase of Abu Sufyan after his raid near Madinah; his men threw away bags of sawiq (barley flour) while fleeing. Uhud, Khandaq and Khaybar were different, bigger battles.
seerah.rel: Sawiq means barley flour. Abu Sufyan made this raid to fulfil his oath after Badr.

seerah.question: In which Islamic month and year did the Battle of Uhud take place?
seerah.facts: Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 AH (March 625 CE). Ramadan 2 AH was Badr, and the other dates do not match any of these battles.
seerah.rel: Battle of the Trench: Shawwal/Dhul Qa'dah 5 AH. Badr: 17 Ramadan 2 AH.

seerah.question: How many Muslims initially set out toward Uhud before a group withdrew?
seerah.facts: About 1,000 Muslims set out; Abdullah ibn Ubayy then left with about 300, leaving about 700. 313 was Badr, 3,000 was the Quraysh army, and 700 is the number left after the withdrawal.
seerah.rel: About 700 Muslims fought at Uhud against 3,000 Quraysh. 313 Muslims fought at Badr.

seerah.question: Approximately how many Quraysh soldiers participated in the Battle of Uhud?
seerah.facts: The Quraysh came to Uhud with about 3,000 soldiers under Abu Sufyan. 1,000 was their number at Badr, and 10,000 was the size of the allied army at the Trench (Ahzab).
seerah.rel: The Quraysh had about 200 horses at Uhud. At the Trench the confederates had about 10,000.

seerah.question: How many archers were positioned to guard the Muslim army's rear at Uhud?
seerah.facts: The Prophet placed 50 archers on the hill of Ainain (Jabal ar-Rumat) to guard the rear. About 10 stayed back when the others left, and 100 and 200 are wrong.
seerah.rel: The archers' hill is called Jabal ar-Rumat (Hill of Archers). Their leader was Abdullah ibn Jubayr.

seerah.question: Who commanded the archers positioned at Uhud?
seerah.facts: Abdullah ibn Jubayr (RA) led the 50 archers and stayed at his post until he was martyred. Mus'ab held the standard, Hamza fought in the main army, and Khalid was then on the Quraysh side.
seerah.rel: Mus'ab ibn Umayr was the standard-bearer at Uhud. Khalid ibn al-Walid accepted Islam in 8 AH.

seerah.question: Which military commander exploited the opening left by archers at Uhud?
seerah.facts: Khalid ibn al-Walid led the Quraysh cavalry around the hill and attacked from behind when the archers left. Abu Sufyan was the overall leader, and Ikrimah helped Khalid but did not lead the attack; Amr ibn al-Aas did not lead it.
seerah.rel: Khalid later got the title Saifullah (Sword of Allah) at Mu'tah. He accepted Islam in 8 AH.

seerah.question: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), the Lion of Allah, was martyred at Uhud?
seerah.facts: Hamza (RA), Asadullah, was martyred at Uhud by Wahshi's spear. Abu Talib died before Hijrah, Abbas lived long after, and Ja'far was a cousin martyred at Mu'tah.
seerah.rel: Hamza is called Sayyid ash-Shuhada (leader of the martyrs). Ja'far is called Ja'far at-Tayyar.

seerah.question: Who was the Muslim standard-bearer martyred at Uhud?
seerah.facts: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) carried the flag at Uhud and was martyred holding it. Ali took the flag after him and survived, Hamza was martyred but not as flag-bearer, and Sa'd was an archer who survived.
seerah.rel: Mus'ab was the first teacher sent to Yathrib. He looked like the Prophet, so some thought the Prophet was killed.

seerah.question: How many Muslims were martyred at the Battle of Uhud according to accounts?
seerah.facts: About 70 Muslims were martyred at Uhud, most of them Ansar. 14 was Badr's number of martyrs, 313 was the Muslim army at Badr, and 100 is not given.
seerah.rel: Quraysh lost about 22-23 men at Uhud. Martyrs of Uhud are buried near Jabal Uhud.

seerah.question: What injury did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sustain during the Battle of Uhud?
seerah.facts: At Uhud a front tooth (lower right) of the Prophet was broken and two rings of his helmet went into his cheek. He did not break his arm, did not lose his sight, and was not unhurt.
seerah.rel: Abu Ubaydah (RA) pulled out the helmet rings with his teeth. Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas threw the stone that hurt the Prophet.

seerah.question: Which companion is remembered for defending Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) at Uhud?
seerah.facts: Talhah (RA) shielded the Prophet with his own body and his hand was paralysed by arrows. Abu Lahab was an enemy who died after Badr, Ibn Ubayy left before the battle, and Musaylimah was a false prophet.
seerah.rel: Talhah is one of the Ashara Mubashara (ten promised Paradise). Abu Dujanah and Nusaybah bint Ka'b also shielded the Prophet at Uhud.

seerah.question: What major lesson is drawn from Uhud regarding the Muslim archers?
options: Obedience to the Prophet (PBUH) was essential
seerah.facts: The archers left their post against the Prophet's clear order, and the Muslims lost the upper hand; so the lesson is obedience. Leaving early caused the loss, cavalry was in fact used against them, and returning to Makkah makes no sense.
seerah.rel: Surah Al-Imran (verses 121-175) discusses Uhud. The archers were told not to leave even if birds snatched the army.
